levels.name: A1 — Beginner
levels.description: First steps in Mandarin: greetings, numbers, basic verbs and questions.

topics.title: Greetings
topics.description: Say hello, goodbye, and how are you

guide.intro: Mandarin has only a handful of greetings to learn — but the tones really matter. Here's what to know before you start.

sections.text: The four tones

Every Mandarin syllable has one of four pitched tones (plus a neutral "fifth" tone). The same syllable means different things depending on tone — so "mā", "má", "mǎ", and "mà" are four different words.
Hello: 你好 (nǐ hǎo)
你 means "you" and 好 means "good". Put them together for "you good?" — the standard hello, usable any time of day.
When two 3rd-tone syllables stack like nǐ hǎo, the first one shifts up to a 2nd tone in speech (ní hǎo). It still gets written as nǐ hǎo.
你 (nǐ) vs 您 (nín)
您 is the polite form of "you" — used with elders, customers, and strangers. 你 is everyday/casual. Both pronounced almost the same.

rows.translation: Hi there.
Hello (formal).
Hello, teacher.

sections.text: How are you?
To turn a statement into a yes/no question, just add 吗 (ma) at the end. So 你好 ("you're good") + 吗 = 你好吗? ("are you good?").

rows.translation: How are you?
I am very good.
Not bad.

lessons.title: Hello & goodbye
lessons.description: The two phrases you can't live without

exercises.prompt: What does "你好" (nǐ hǎo) mean?
How do you say "goodbye"?
"再见" (zài jiàn) means ___
exercises.explanation: "再见" literally means "see you again."

exercises.prompt: the greeting to its meaning
Tap the phrase you hear
exercises.explanation: 你好 (nǐ hǎo) is the everyday hello — both syllables third tone, but the first becomes second tone in speech.

exercises.prompt: You meet your friend's grandmother for the first time. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 您 (nín) is the polite "you" — used with elders, customers, and strangers to show respect.

exercises.prompt: "明天见" (míng tiān jiàn) means "see you ___"
exercises.explanation: 见 (jiàn) means "see/meet" — pair it with a time word to schedule a goodbye.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Hello, Teacher!"
exercises.explanation: Putting 老师 first is a respectful way to address a teacher before the greeting.

exercises.prompt: Which is NOT a way to say goodbye?
exercises.explanation: 拜拜 (bài bài) is borrowed from English "bye-bye" and is very common in casual speech.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
"拜拜" (bài bài) means ___
exercises.explanation: Borrowed from English — common in informal goodbyes, especially over the phone.

lessons.title: How are you?
lessons.description: Ask after someone and answer back

exercises.prompt: How do you say "How are you?"
What does "很好" (hěn hǎo) mean?
Tap the phrase you hear
Build: "I'm very good, thank you."
exercises.answer: 我 很 好 谢谢
exercises.explanation: In Mandarin, adjectives don't take 是 — "I am good" is literally 我很好 (I very good).

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks 你好吗? You're feeling fine. What do you say?
"不错" (bú cuò) literally "not wrong" — it means ___
exercises.explanation: Common, slightly understated way to answer "how are you?" — like English "not bad."

exercises.prompt: the response with its tone
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: Listen for 我 (wǒ, third tone — dipping) vs 你 (nǐ) and 他 (tā).

exercises.prompt: What does "你呢" (nǐ ne) mean?
exercises.explanation: 呢 (ne) bounces a question back. After answering 我很好, add 你呢 to ask the same of the other person.

exercises.prompt: Build: "How are you? And you?" — answer the first question with "and you?"
exercises.answer: 我 很 好 你 呢

exercises.prompt: "马马虎虎" (mǎ mǎ hū hū) literally "horse horse tiger tiger" means ___
exercises.explanation: A fun idiom — when neither good nor bad, you're "horse-tiger."

lessons.title: Polite phrases
lessons.description: Thank you, sorry, and you're welcome

exercises.prompt: How do you say "thank you"?
What does "对不起" mean?
"不客气" (bú kè qi) means ___
exercises.explanation: Literally "don't be polite" — the standard reply to 谢谢.

exercises.prompt: each polite phrase
Someone says 对不起 to you. What's the natural reply?
exercises.explanation: 没关系 (méi guān xi) means "it doesn't matter / it's okay" — the standard answer to an apology.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
"请" (qǐng) means ___
exercises.explanation: Place 请 at the start of a request to be polite, e.g. 请坐 (please sit).

exercises.prompt: What does "请坐" (qǐng zuò) mean?
Build: "Sorry, thank you."
Which is more emphatic for "thank you very much"?
exercises.explanation: 非常 (fēi cháng) = extremely; 感谢 (gǎn xiè) is a more formal "thanks." Together: "thanks a lot."

exercises.prompt: "没关系" (méi guān xi) means ___
Build: "Sorry, please wait a moment"
exercises.answer: 对不起 请 等 一下

lessons.title: Nice to meet you
lessons.description: Introduce yourself

exercises.prompt: What does "我叫" (wǒ jiào) mean?
Build: "I am called Xiao Ming"
"认识你很高兴" means ___
exercises.explanation: Literally: "knowing you makes me happy."

exercises.prompt: What does "你叫什么名字" mean?
exercises.explanation: Literally: "You called what name?" 名字 (míng zi) = name.

exercises.prompt: Build: "What is your name?"
exercises.answer: 你 叫 什么 名字

exercises.prompt: the introduction phrase
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 我叫 (wǒ jiào) — "I am called." Listen for the falling tone on 叫.

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between "我叫小明" and "我是小明"?
options: Both mean "my name is Xiao Ming" — 叫 is more common in casual intros
我叫 means "I want" and 我是 means "I am"
我叫 is past tense, 我是 is present tense
exercises.answer: Both mean "my name is Xiao Ming" — 叫 is more common in casual intros
exercises.explanation: 我叫 literally "I'm called" — natural, friendly. 我是 literally "I am" — slightly more formal.

exercises.prompt: "贵姓" (guì xìng) literally "honored surname" — used to ask ___
exercises.explanation: Polite way to ask someone's last name: 您贵姓? Reply with 我姓 + your surname.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Nice to meet you" (literally: meeting you very happy)
exercises.answer: 认识 你 很 高兴

exercises.prompt: You meet someone new. They say 你好, 我叫王明. What do you say back?
options: 你好, 我叫... 认识你很高兴
exercises.answer: 你好, 我叫... 认识你很高兴
exercises.explanation: Mirror the greeting and add "nice to meet you" — that's the standard A1 introduction.

lessons.title: Dialogue: First day at school
lessons.description: Meet a new classmate and exchange greetings.

exercises.prompt: Meeting a classmate on your first day

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 你好！(nǐ hǎo)
turns.spokenText: 你好！

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Say hello back.
turns.answer: 你好！(nǐ hǎo)

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 你好吗？(nǐ hǎo ma)
turns.spokenText: 你好吗？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Say you are very good.
turns.answer: 我很好。(wǒ hěn hǎo)

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 我叫小明。(wǒ jiào Xiǎo Míng)
turns.spokenText: 我叫小明。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in: I'm called Lì.
turns.answer: 叫

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 认识你很高兴。(rèn shi nǐ hěn gāo xìng)
turns.spokenText: 认识你很高兴。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Say goodbye.
turns.answer: 再见！(zài jiàn)

topics.title: Numbers
topics.description: Count, ask how many, give your age

guide.intro: Mandarin numbers are wonderfully regular — once you know 1 to 10 and the word for "ten", you can build every number up to 99.

sections.text: One to ten
Building 11–99
After ten, numbers are built like math problems. Read characters left to right, multiplying anything before 十 and adding anything after.
Same trick goes further: 一百 (one hundred), 一千 (one thousand), 一万 (ten thousand) — but Chinese groups large numbers in 万 (10,000) rather than thousands.
Two: 二 vs 两
Mandarin has two words for "two". 二 (èr) is the digit — used in counting, math, and phone numbers. 两 (liǎng) means "a pair of" — used before measure words and quantities.

rows.translation: twenty (the number)
two people (with measure word)

sections.text: Asking how many
几 (jǐ) asks "how many?" for small expected counts (under ~10). 多少 (duō shǎo) asks "how much/many?" for any quantity, including money and big numbers.

rows.translation: How old are you? (to a child)
How much money?

lessons.title: One to five
lessons.description: Count from 一 to 五

exercises.prompt: What is "三" (sān)?
How do you write "five"?
the digit
Which is "two"?
"四" (sì) means ___
exercises.explanation: 四 sounds similar to 死 (sǐ, "death") — for this reason 4 is sometimes considered unlucky in Chinese culture, like 13 in the West.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 三 (sān) — first tone, high and flat. Don't confuse with 四 (sì), fourth tone, sharp falling.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 四 (sì) is fourth tone — sharp falling. Compare to 三 (sān), high and flat.

exercises.prompt: Which two numbers sound similar but differ only in tone?
exercises.explanation: Both have the same final "-ān/-ì" feel — distinguish by tone: 三 high-flat, 四 sharp-falling.

exercises.prompt: Order the numbers from one to five
exercises.answer: 一 二 三 四 五

exercises.prompt: Which character means "one"?
exercises.explanation: Just one stroke — the simplest character in Chinese.

exercises.prompt: "五" (wǔ) means ___
Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 二 (èr) — fourth tone, sharp falling. Quick to say.

lessons.title: Six to ten
lessons.description: Count up to 十

exercises.prompt: What is "六" (liù)?
What is "九" (jiǔ)?
"十" (shí) means ___
digit to character
Which is "seven"?
Which is "eight"?
exercises.explanation: 八 (bā) sounds like 发 (fā, "to prosper") — making 8 the luckiest number in Chinese culture.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 九 (jiǔ) is third tone — dipping. Long and dramatic compared to other tones.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 十 (shí) is second tone — rising. Don't confuse with 四 (sì), fourth tone.

exercises.prompt: Order the numbers from six to ten
exercises.answer: 六 七 八 九 十

exercises.prompt: Which number is considered the luckiest in Chinese culture?
exercises.explanation: 八 (bā) rhymes with 发 (fā, "to prosper"). Phone numbers and license plates with many 8s sell at a premium.

exercises.prompt: "六" (liù) means ___
Order the digits in ascending order: 8, 6, 9, 7
exercises.answer: 六 七 八 九

lessons.title: Tens and beyond
lessons.description: Build bigger numbers

exercises.prompt: What is "二十" (èr shí)?
How do you write "fifteen"?
exercises.explanation: 十五 = 10 + 5. Order matters!

exercises.prompt: Build "thirty-three"
What is "七十二" (qī shí èr)?
exercises.explanation: Read left to right: 七 (7) × 十 (10) + 二 (2) = 72.

exercises.prompt: "九十九" (jiǔ shí jiǔ) is the number ___
How do you write "forty-five"?
exercises.explanation: 四十 = 40, then add 五 = 45. The pattern: tens-digit + 十 + units-digit.

exercises.prompt: the number
Build "sixty-eight"
What is "一百" (yì bǎi)?
exercises.explanation: 百 (bǎi) is the unit for hundreds — 一百 = 100, 二百 = 200.

exercises.prompt: Tap the number you hear
exercises.explanation: Listen for the order: 二十一 = 21 ("two-ten-one"), 十二 = 12 ("ten-two").

exercises.prompt: Build the number "twelve" — order matters!
exercises.explanation: 十二 = 10 + 2. Compare: 二十 = 2 × 10 = 20. The order of 十 and the digit reverses the meaning.

exercises.prompt: "五十" (wǔ shí) is the number ___

lessons.title: How old? How many?
lessons.description: Use numbers in real questions

exercises.prompt: What does "几岁" (jǐ suì) mean?
"五岁" means ___ years old
What does "多少" (duō shǎo) mean?
Use 几 or 多少? "How many people are in your family?"
options: 多少 — could be a big number
exercises.explanation: 几 (jǐ) for under ~10, things you can count on fingers. 多少 (duō shǎo) for any quantity, including money and large numbers.

exercises.prompt: Build: "How old are you?" (to a child)
exercises.explanation: 几岁 is for kids; for adults use 你多大?

exercises.prompt: "我二十岁" means "I am ___ years old"
exercises.explanation: No 是 needed — 我二十岁, not 我是二十岁. Age uses adjective-like structure.

exercises.prompt: Which question would you ask an adult their age?
exercises.explanation: 几岁 is for children. 多大 (literally "how big") is the polite ask for adults.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 多少钱 (duō shǎo qián) — "how much money?" The phrase you'll use most when shopping.

exercises.prompt: the question word
Build: "I have three older brothers"
exercises.answer: 我 有 三 个 哥哥
exercises.explanation: Numbers always need a measure word before a noun: 三个哥哥, not 三哥哥.

lessons.title: Phone numbers & dates
lessons.description: Read digits one at a time

exercises.prompt: When reading a phone number aloud, how is each digit spoken?
options: One digit at a time, like "yī sān bā"
Grouped as full numbers, like "yī bǎi sān shí bā"
Skipped — only key ones are said
exercises.answer: One digit at a time, like "yī sān bā"
exercises.explanation: Phone numbers, addresses, and ID numbers are read digit-by-digit — same as in English.

exercises.prompt: When dictating a phone number, the digit "1" is often pronounced as ___ instead of "yī"
exercises.explanation: 幺 (yāo) replaces 一 (yī) in spoken digit strings to avoid confusing 一 with 七 (qī). You'll hear it on the phone and at the bank.

exercises.prompt: "零" (líng) means ___
exercises.explanation: 零 is the formal zero. You'll also see 〇 (a circle) used in dates and ID numbers.

exercises.prompt: the digit
How do you say "the year 2024"?
exercises.explanation: Years are read digit-by-digit + 年 (nián, year). 二零二四年 = "two-zero-two-four year."

exercises.prompt: "月" (yuè) means ___
exercises.explanation: 月 by itself means moon/month. With a number: 一月 = January, 二月 = February.

exercises.prompt: Which is "March"?
exercises.explanation: Months are number + 月. 三月 = March (3rd month). Don't confuse 月 (month) with 日 (day).

exercises.prompt: Build the date: "May 6th" (5月 then day-number then 号)
exercises.answer: 五 月 六 号
exercises.explanation: 号 (hào) is the casual word for date/day. 日 (rì) is the formal equivalent — both follow the day number.

exercises.prompt: Tap the date you hear
exercises.explanation: Big to small: 六月 (June) comes before 十号 (10th). Don't reverse it like English "the 10th of June."

exercises.prompt: Chinese dates go in what order?
exercises.explanation: Chinese always reads dates from largest unit to smallest: 2024年5月6日. Same logic for time: hour first, minute last.

exercises.prompt: "今天几月几号?" asks ___
exercises.explanation: Literally: "Today which month, which date?" The everyday way to ask the date.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear

lessons.title: Dialogue: At the fruit market
lessons.description: Count fruit and ask how much things cost.

exercises.prompt: Buying apples at a market stand

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 你好！(nǐ hǎo)
turns.spokenText: 你好！

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Ask how much (the apples cost).
turns.answer: 多少钱？(duō shao qián)

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 五块钱一个。(wǔ kuài qián yí ge)
turns.spokenText: 五块钱一个。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in the measure word: I want three (apples).
turns.answer: 个

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 三个十五块。(sān ge shí wǔ kuài)
turns.spokenText: 三个十五块。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Hand over the money — say 'here you go'.
turns.answer: 给你。(gěi nǐ)

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 谢谢，再见！(xiè xie, zài jiàn)
turns.spokenText: 谢谢，再见！

topics.title: Basics
topics.description: Yes, no, I, you, this, that

guide.intro: Mandarin has no verb conjugation, no plural endings, no genders, and no articles. Once you know the word order, the language gets out of your way.

sections.text: Word order: subject – verb – object
Just like English, a basic sentence puts the subject first, the verb second, and the object last.

rows.translation: I drink tea.
He eats rice.
I love you.

sections.text: Pronouns are simple
他 (he) and 她 (she) are pronounced exactly the same — only the writing changes. In speech, listeners use context.
The verb 是 (shì)
是 means "to be" — but only for nouns connecting to other nouns ("I am a student"). For adjectives, you don't use 是; you use 很 (hěn) instead, which means "very" but is often a placeholder.

rows.translation: I am a student.
I am good. (no 是!)

sections.text: Negation: 不 vs 没
Use 不 (bù) for negating present and future actions, and for adjectives. Use 没 (méi) for past actions and for the verb 有 ("to have").

rows.source: 我 不 喝 茶。
rows.translation: I don't drink tea.

rows.source: 我 没 有 钱。
rows.translation: I don't have money.

sections.text: No tenses!
Mandarin verbs do not change form for past, present, or future. Time is shown by adding a time word (yesterday, tomorrow) or particles like 了 (le) for completion.

rows.source: 昨天 我 吃 米饭。
rows.translation: Yesterday I ate rice.

rows.source: 明天 我 吃 米饭。
rows.translation: Tomorrow I will eat rice.

lessons.title: Yes & no
lessons.description: Simple yes/no responses

exercises.prompt: How do you say "yes"?
Which character means "no" / "not"?
"不是" (bú shì) means ___
exercises.explanation: "不是" literally "is not" — a common way to say "no".

exercises.prompt: Mandarin has no single word for "yes/no." Instead, you reply with the ___
options: Verb itself, optionally negated with 不
exercises.answer: Verb itself, optionally negated with 不
exercises.explanation: Q: 你喝茶吗? (Do you drink tea?) → A: 喝 (yes, drink) or 不喝 (no, don't drink). Mirror the verb.

exercises.prompt: the right negation: ___ 喝 茶。(I don't drink tea.)
exercises.explanation: 不 (bù) negates present/future and adjectives. 没 (méi) is for past actions and 有.

exercises.prompt: the right negation: 我 ___ 有 钱。(I don't have money.)
exercises.explanation: 有 (have) is the one verb that's always negated with 没, never 不. 没有 is fixed.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I am not a student"
exercises.answer: 我 不 是 学生

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 不 before a fourth tone (是, shì) shifts to second tone — pronounced "bú shì."

exercises.prompt: "对" (duì) literally "correct" — used like ___
exercises.explanation: 对 is the closest word to a casual "yes" — confirms what someone said. Reverse: 不对 ("no, that's wrong").

exercises.prompt: Build a negative reply to 你是中国人吗? — "I am not Chinese"
exercises.answer: 我 不 是 中国 人
exercises.explanation: Mirror the verb 是 in the question and negate with 不: 不是. Don't add a separate "no" word.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 我没有 = "I don't have." 没 always pairs with 有, never 不.

lessons.title: I & you
lessons.description: Basic pronouns

exercises.prompt: What does "我" (wǒ) mean?
What does "你" (nǐ) mean?
"我们" (wǒ men) means ___
exercises.explanation: Add "们" to make a plural pronoun: 我们 = we.

exercises.prompt: What does "你们" (nǐ men) mean?
exercises.explanation: 你 + 们 = you (plural). English doesn't always distinguish singular/plural "you," but Mandarin does.

exercises.prompt: the pronoun
Build: "We are good"
exercises.explanation: Adjectives don't take 是 — 我们很好, not 我们是好.

exercises.prompt: What does "您" (nín) mean?
exercises.explanation: 您 is the formal "you" for elders, customers, strangers. The character has a 心 (heart) under 你 — "you with my heart."

exercises.prompt: The polite form of 你 is ___
exercises.explanation: 您 is used in shops, on the phone, with elders. Don't use it with close friends — feels stiff.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 我们 (wǒ men) — listen for the third tone on 我.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I am Chinese"?
options: 我们 是 中国人
我 不 是 中国人

exercises.prompt: Build: "You all are my friends"
exercises.answer: 你们 是 我 的 朋友
exercises.explanation: 的 (de) makes a possessive: 我的 = "my," 你的 = "your."

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 您 (nín) — second tone, similar to 你 (nǐ, third tone). Listen for the rising vs dipping pitch.

lessons.title: He, she, they
lessons.description: Talk about other people

exercises.prompt: What does "他" (tā) mean?
What does "她" (tā) mean?
the pronoun
他 (he) and 她 (she) — what's the difference?
options: Different meanings (one is for adults, one for kids)
exercises.explanation: In speech, you can't tell — context decides. The 女 radical in 她 marks female; 它 (also tā) is for animals/things.

exercises.prompt: "他们" (tā men) means ___
exercises.explanation: 他们 is used for groups that are mixed-gender or all-male. 她们 is used only for all-female groups.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun is used for animals or inanimate objects?
exercises.explanation: 它 (tā) — same pronunciation as 他/她 but written with the radical 宀 (roof). Use it for pets, things, weather.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 他们 (tā men) — first tone on 他, neutral on 们. In speech, identical to 她们.

exercises.prompt: Build: "She is my older sister"
exercises.answer: 她 是 我 姐姐

exercises.prompt: A group of three women — which is correct?
exercises.explanation: All-female groups use 她们. Add a single male and most speakers switch to 他们.

exercises.prompt: "她" is written with the radical ___ to mark female
exercises.explanation: 女 (nǚ) means "woman" — placed on the left side of 她 to distinguish it from 他.

exercises.prompt: Build: "They drink tea"
The pronoun for animals/things is ___
exercises.explanation: 它 (tā) — same sound as 他 and 她, but a different character. Use for pets, weather, things.

lessons.title: This & that
lessons.description: Point things out

exercises.prompt: What does "这" (zhè) mean?
What does "那" (nà) mean?
Build "This is my mom"
exercises.answer: 这 是 我 妈妈

exercises.prompt: What does "这个" (zhè ge) mean?
exercises.explanation: 个 (ge) is the all-purpose measure word. 这个 = "this (item)," 那个 = "that (item)."

exercises.prompt: the pointer
"那个" (nà ge) means ___
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 这 (zhè) — fourth tone, sharp falling. 那 (nà) is also fourth tone but starts with "n."

topics.title: Common verbs
topics.description: Go, eat, want, like, see, listen

guide.intro: Mandarin verbs never change form. The same character is used for all persons and all times — context (and time words) does the heavy lifting.

sections.text: One verb, every form
Compare with English: "go / goes / went / will go" — Mandarin uses 去 for all of them. The action stays put; you add words around it.

rows.translation: I go / I am going.
He goes.
We go.
I went yesterday.

sections.text: Want vs. would-like: 要 / 想 / 喜欢
These three look interchangeable in English but have a clear pecking order in Mandarin.

rows: I want / I will (decisive, ordering food)
I would like / I am thinking about

rows.translation: I want coffee. (I'll have)

rows.source: 我 想 喝 咖啡。
rows.translation: I would like to drink coffee.
I like coffee.

sections.text: Completion: the 了 particle
Adding 了 (le) after a verb signals an action is finished. It's the closest thing Mandarin has to past tense — but it's really an aspect marker, not a tense.

rows.translation: I am eating.

rows.source: 我 吃 了 饭。
rows.translation: I ate. / I have eaten.

sections.text: Don't sprinkle 了 everywhere — for adjectives ("I am happy") or stative verbs, you don't use it. Save it for completed actions.

exercises.prompt: What does "喜欢" (xǐ huan) mean?

Pick the right verb: ordering at a café — "I'll have a coffee."
options: 我要 一 杯 咖啡
我想 一 杯 咖啡
我喜欢 一 杯 咖啡
我有 一 杯 咖啡
exercises.answer: 我要 一 杯 咖啡
exercises.explanation: 要 (yào) is decisive — "I want / I'll have." Use it when ordering. 想 (xiǎng) is softer ("would like").

exercises.prompt: Pick the right verb: "I'd like to drink tea." (softer wish)

杯 is not a measure word
exercises.answer: 喜欢 means general preference, not a one-time order
exercises.explanation: 喜欢 = "I like coffee in general." To order one cup, use 要: 我要一杯咖啡.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 想 (xiǎng, third tone) — listen for the dipping pitch. Don't confuse with 要 (yào, fourth tone falling).

exercises.prompt: When ordering at a restaurant, the most natural verb is ___
exercises.explanation: 要 (yào) signals decisive intent — perfect for ordering. 想 sounds more like "considering it."

topics.title: Time
topics.description: Days, hours, and when things happen

guide.intro: Time words go at the start of a sentence or right after the subject — never at the end like English. "Tomorrow I go" is the natural Mandarin order.

sections.text: Days are math
Days of the week are 星期 (xīngqī, "week") + the digit. So 星期一 is week-1 (Monday), 星期二 is week-2 (Tuesday), and so on through 星期六. Sunday is the odd one out: 星期天 or 星期日.
Telling time
Hours use 点 (diǎn, "o'clock"), minutes use 分 (fēn). Half-past is 半 (bàn). "Quarter" is 一刻 (yí kè) for :15 and 三刻 for :45.

rows.translation: 3 o'clock

sections.text: Time-words come first
In Mandarin, time goes before the verb. Compare:

rows.source: 我 明天 去 学校。
rows.translation: I am going to school tomorrow.

rows.source: 他 今天 不 来。
rows.translation: He is not coming today.

sections.text: A handy memory trick: Chinese says time in big-to-small order — year, month, day, hour, minute. The opposite of how dates are spoken in English.

By adding 是 before the verb

topics.title: Questions
topics.description: Who, what, when, why, how

guide.intro: Mandarin questions are unusually friendly to learners — there's no auxiliary "do/does", no inversion. The word order stays the same as a statement.

sections.text: The 吗 particle
For yes/no questions, take a statement and add 吗 (ma) at the end. That's it. No reordering, no auxiliary verb.

rows.translation: You drink tea.

rows.source: 你 喝 茶 吗？
rows.translation: Do you drink tea?

sections.text: Question words stay put
For information questions (who, what, where), put the question word exactly where the answer would go. No fronting like English.

rows.translation: Who are you? (You are who?)
What are you drinking?
Where are you?
Why is he coming?

sections.text: Common question words
A-not-A questions
A second way to ask yes/no questions: repeat the verb with 不 between. It's a touch more direct than 吗.

rows.source: 你 是不是 学生？
rows.translation: Are you a student or not?
Do you drink tea or not?

sections.text: Don't mix patterns: 你是不是学生吗？ is wrong. Pick one of the two question forms.

topics.title: Completed actions
topics.description: 了 for what just happened, 过 for what you've ever done

guide.intro: A1 introduced 了 briefly. A2 is where it really earns its keep. There are also two siblings to learn — 过 (experience) and 还没 (not yet) — that round out talking about the past.

sections.text: 了 — completed action
Tack 了 onto a verb to mark that the action is finished. It's the closest thing Mandarin has to a past tense, but technically it's an aspect marker — the action is complete, not necessarily long ago.

rows.translation: I am eating.

rows.source: 我 吃 了 饭。
rows.translation: I ate / I have eaten.
He came / he's here.

sections.text: Negation: 还没 (not yet)
Don't pair 了 with 不/没. To say "haven't done it", drop 了 and use 还没 (hái méi):

rows.translation: I haven't eaten yet.
He hasn't come yet.

sections.text: 过 — experience marker
过 (guò) tags a verb as "have you ever done this in your life?" — it's about experience, not completion. Compare:

rows.source: 我 吃 过 北京 烤鸭。
rows.translation: I have eaten Peking duck (sometime).

rows.source: 我 吃 了 北京 烤鸭。
rows.translation: I ate Peking duck (just now).

sections.text: Rule of thumb: 了 = the action is wrapped up. 过 = at some point in your life this happened. They occasionally co-occur but you'll mostly pick one.

topics.title: Shopping
topics.description: Money, prices, and getting what you want

guide.intro: Real Chinese shopping is fast and friendly. Three phrases get you 80% of the way there: 多少钱 (how much), 太贵了 (too expensive), and 给我 (give me).

sections.text: Money words
Spoken Chinese uses 块 (kuài) for the main currency unit; written and formal Chinese uses 元 (yuán). They're the same value — like "buck" vs "dollar". 毛 (máo) and 分 (fēn) are tenths and hundredths.

topics.title: Comparisons
topics.description: A is bigger than B — the 比 pattern

guide.intro: English uses "-er" or "more" for comparisons. Mandarin uses 比 (bǐ) — a single particle that does the same job, with a fixed word order: A 比 B + adjective.

sections.text: Basic pattern: A 比 B + adjective

rows.source: 我 比 他 高。
rows.translation: I am taller than him.

rows.source: 苹果 比 香蕉 便宜。
rows.translation: Apples are cheaper than bananas.

rows.source: 今天 比 昨天 热。
rows.translation: Today is hotter than yesterday.

sections.text: Don't add 很 / 不 / 是 to a 比 sentence. "我 比 他 很 高" is wrong — drop 很. The comparison itself does the work.
Even more: 更
Add 更 (gèng, "even more") before the adjective when comparing to an already-strong baseline:

rows.source: 他 比 我 更 高。
rows.translation: He is even taller than me.

sections.text: The most: 最
最 (zuì) before an adjective means "the most". No 比 needed — it's a superlative.

rows.translation: He is the tallest.

rows.source: 我 最 喜欢 茶。
rows.translation: I like tea the most.

sections.text: Negative: A 没有 B + adjective
To say "A is NOT as ___ as B", flip to 没有 (méi yǒu, "doesn't have"):

rows.source: 我 没有 他 高。
rows.translation: I am not as tall as him.

topics.title: Connecting ideas
topics.description: And, but, because, so — stitch sentences together

guide.intro: Up to now most sentences have been one thought. A2 is where you start chaining: "I went and then I ate", "It rained but I went", "I'm tired because I worked". Mandarin makes this easy — a small set of connectors does most of the heavy lifting.

sections.text: 然后 — and then
然后 (rán hòu) chains two events in time. Use it to narrate sequences.

rows.source: 我 起床，然后 吃 早饭。
rows.translation: I get up, and then I eat breakfast.

sections.text: 但是 / 可是 — but
Both mean "but" with no real difference; 可是 is a touch more conversational.

rows.source: 我 想 去，但是 我 没 时间。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì wǒ méi shíjiān.
rows.translation: I want to go, but I don't have time.

sections.text: 因为...所以 — because...so
Mandarin often uses both halves where English uses just one ("I'm tired BECAUSE I worked" → 因为 我 工作 了，所以 我 很 累).

rows.source: 因为 下雨，所以 我 没 去。
rows.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù.
rows.translation: Because it was raining, (so) I didn't go.

sections.text: You can drop one half if context is clear: "因为 下雨，我 没 去" works too. The full pair just sounds slightly more emphatic.
或者 vs 还是 — both mean "or"
Easy mix-up. 或者 (huò zhě) goes in statements ("I want tea or coffee"). 还是 (hái shi) goes in questions ("Do you want tea or coffee?").

rows.source: 我 想 喝 茶 或者 咖啡。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hē chá huòzhě kāfēi.
rows.translation: I want to drink tea or coffee. (statement)

rows.source: 你 想 喝 茶 还是 咖啡？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi kāfēi?
rows.translation: Do you want tea or coffee? (choice question)

topics.title: The 把 construction
topics.description: Putting the object first to talk about what you do TO it

guide.intro: 把 (bǎ) is one of the most distinctive features of Mandarin grammar. It moves the object before the verb to say "take X and do something to it". You'll hear it constantly — and English doesn't have a clean equivalent.

sections.text: The basic shape

Normal Chinese order is Subject–Verb–Object. With 把, you reorder to Subject–把–Object–Verb–(extra). The "extra" part is crucial — 把 sentences almost never end on a bare verb. There has to be a result, location, or change attached.

rows: 我 把 门 关 上
他 把 苹果 吃 了
请 放 书 在 桌子 上
请 把 书 放 在 桌子 上

sections.text: When to use 把
Use 把 when you want to emphasize what HAPPENS TO a specific, known object — moving it, finishing it, changing it, putting it somewhere. Both speaker and listener know which object you mean.

rows.source: 我 把 作业 做 完 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le.
rows.translation: I finished the homework.

rows.source: 请 把 窗户 打 开。
rows.translation: Please open the window.

rows.source: 他 把 杯子 打 破 了。
rows.pinyin: Tā bǎ bēizi dǎ pò le.
rows.translation: He broke the cup.

sections.text: If you can't say what HAPPENS TO the object, don't use 把. "我 把 苹果 喜欢" is wrong — 喜欢 (like) doesn't change the apple.
What can't follow 把
把 needs a verb that physically affects the object. Verbs that don't qualify: feeling/perception verbs (爱, 喜欢, 觉得, 知道), existence verbs (有, 是), and most stative or motion-only verbs (来, 去, 走).

rows.source: 我 喜欢 这 本 书。
rows.translation: I like this book. (NOT 我 把 这 本 书 喜欢)
He knows the answer. (NOT 他 把 答案 知道)

sections.text: Negation: 没 / 不 goes BEFORE 把

rows.source: 我 没 把 作业 做 完。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ méi bǎ zuòyè zuò wán.
rows.translation: I didn't finish the homework.

rows.source: 请 不要 把 门 关 上。
rows.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào bǎ mén guān shàng.

topics.title: The 被 passive
topics.description: When something happens TO the subject — usually unpleasantly

guide.intro: 被 (bèi) is the passive marker — "got / was done by". It's the mirror image of 把: where 把 puts the actor first and the patient mid-sentence, 被 puts the patient (victim) first.

sections.text: The basic shape
Pattern: Patient + 被 + (Agent) + Verb + result. The agent is optional — drop it if it's unknown or obvious.

rows.source: 我 的 手机 被 偷 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
rows.translation: My phone was stolen. (no agent)

rows.source: 杯子 被 他 打 破 了。
rows.pinyin: Bēizi bèi tā dǎ pò le.
rows.translation: The cup was broken by him.

rows.source: 钱 被 老板 拿走 了。
rows.pinyin: Qián bèi lǎobǎn ná zǒu le.
rows.translation: The money was taken by the boss.

sections.text: 把 vs 被 — same event, different POV

rows: 他 把 杯子 打 破 了
杯子 被 他 打 破 了
小偷 偷 了 我 的 手机
我 的 手机 被 (小偷) 偷 了

sections.text: Mandarin's 被 has a slightly negative or unfortunate flavor — it's used much more often for bad things (got stolen, broken, scolded) than for neutral or good ones. Sentences like "I was praised" (我 被 表扬 了) work but feel marked.
叫 / 让 — informal alternatives
In speech, 叫 (jiào) or 让 (ràng) often replace 被. They sound more casual — but unlike 被, they REQUIRE an agent.

rows.source: 我 的 钱 让 他 拿走 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de qián ràng tā ná zǒu le.
rows.translation: My money got taken by him.

rows.source: 他 叫 老师 批评 了。
rows.translation: He got scolded by the teacher.

sections.text: Negation
Same as 把 — put 没 BEFORE 被.

rows.source: 我 的 手机 没 被 偷。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi bèi tōu.
rows.translation: My phone wasn't stolen.

sections.text: Two flavors of 了
Mandarin uses 了 in two distinct slots, and 把 / 被 sentences often need both. Knowing which is which is the difference between a complete sentence and a fragment.

rows: Something is now different / new situation

rows.source: 他 吃 了 三 个 苹果。
rows.pinyin: Tā chī le sān ge píngguǒ.
rows.translation: He ate three apples. (perfective 了₁ — action complete)
It's raining now. (sentence 了₂ — change of state, didn't use to be)

rows.source: 已经 下 了 三 天 雨 了。
rows.pinyin: Yǐjīng xià le sān tiān yǔ le.
rows.translation: It's been raining for three days. (BOTH 了 — completed duration AND ongoing relevance)

sections.text: Quick test: if the 了 hugs the verb (verb 了 object), it's 了₁. If the 了 is at the very end of the sentence, it's 了₂. Same character, different jobs.

topics.title: Giving with 给
topics.description: 给 as both "give" and a coverb meaning "for / to"

guide.intro: 给 (gěi) wears two hats. As a main verb it means "give". As a coverb sitting before another verb, it marks the recipient or beneficiary — "for someone", "to someone". Both uses are everywhere.

sections.text: 给 as main verb — "give"
Pattern: Subject + 给 + recipient + thing. Two objects in a row, recipient first.

rows.source: 我 给 他 一 本 书。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā yì běn shū.
rows.translation: I gave him a book.

rows.source: 妈妈 给 我 钱。
rows.translation: Mom gave me money.

sections.text: 给 as coverb — "for / to"
Sandwiched before another verb, 给 marks who benefits or receives the action. Pattern: Subject + 给 + recipient + verb + object.

rows.source: 我 给 你 买 了 一 杯 咖啡。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ mǎi le yì bēi kāfēi.
rows.translation: I bought you a coffee. (the buying is FOR you)

rows.source: 他 给 妈妈 打 电话。
rows.translation: He's calling mom. (the call is TO mom)

rows.source: 请 给 我 介绍 一下。
rows.translation: Please introduce (it) to me.

sections.text: Notice how 给 you 买 (buy for you) and 给 妈妈 打 电话 (call mom) both keep 给 + person BEFORE the main verb. English flips this around — Chinese is rigid about the order.

topics.title: How well? — 得 complement
topics.description: Modify a verb with how it was done — 得 + adjective

guide.intro: 得 (de) lets you describe the manner or degree of an action: not WHAT you did, but HOW WELL or HOW MUCH. It's the closest Mandarin gets to English adverbs.

sections.text: The basic pattern
Pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + (very) + Adjective. Note the position of 很 — almost always required to keep the sentence sounding natural.

rows.source: 他 跑 得 很 快。
rows.translation: He runs very fast.

rows.source: 她 唱 得 很 好。
rows.translation: She sings very well.

rows.source: 我 睡 得 不 好。
rows.translation: I didn't sleep well.

sections.text: When the verb has an object
If your verb takes an object, you have to repeat the verb. Mandarin can't have an object AND a 得 phrase on the same verb. Pattern: Subject + Verb + Object, Verb + 得 + adjective.

rows.source: 他 说 中文 说 得 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: He speaks Chinese very well. (literally: "speaks Chinese, speaks very well")

rows.source: 她 写 字 写 得 很 漂亮。
rows.pinyin: Tā xiě zì xiě de hěn piàoliang.
rows.translation: She writes characters beautifully.

sections.text: Common mistake: "他 说 中文 得 很 好" — wrong. The verb has to repeat. Or you can drop the object: "他 中文 说 得 很 好" also works.
Three different 得 / 的 / 地

rows: after a verb: how it was done
走 得 慢 — walks slowly

sections.text: All three are pronounced "de" (neutral tone) — only writing distinguishes them. Pay attention to position: 的 between nouns, 地 before verbs, 得 after verbs.
Negation: not 不 before 得 — 不 before the adjective

rows.source: 他 跑 得 不 快。
rows.translation: He doesn't run fast.

rows.source: 我 唱 得 不 好。
rows.translation: I don't sing well.

topics.title: Opinions & agreement
topics.description: I think, I believe, I agree — saying what you reckon

guide.intro: B1 means saying more than "I like" or "I want". You need ways to express opinions softly, agree, disagree, and ask people what THEY think. Three verbs do the heavy lifting: 觉得, 认为, and 看.

sections.text: 觉得 — feel / think (everyday)
觉得 (jué de) is the workhorse — "I feel / think that...". Use it for any soft, personal opinion. By far the most common in conversation.

rows.source: 我 觉得 这 个 电影 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè ge diànyǐng hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: I think this movie is good.

rows.source: 你 觉得 怎么样？
rows.translation: What do you think?

sections.text: 认为 — believe / hold (more formal)
认为 (rèn wéi) is firmer and more written — "I hold the view that...". Right for opinions on bigger issues, news, business, debate.

rows.source: 我 认为 这 个 计划 不 行。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi zhè ge jìhuà bù xíng.
rows.translation: I don't think this plan will work.

rows.source: 专家 认为 经济 会 好转。
rows.translation: Experts believe the economy will improve.

sections.text: 看 — see / view (informal opinion ask)
看 (kàn) literally means "look", but "你 看 …" idiomatically means "in your view, …". Used to gently ask someone's take.

rows.source: 你 看 我 该 怎么 办？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ kàn wǒ gāi zěnme bàn?
rows.translation: What do you think I should do?

rows.source: 我 看 应该 没 问题。
rows.translation: I think it should be fine.

sections.text: Agreeing & disagreeing
Chinese conversation tends to soften disagreement. "我 不 太 同意" (I don't really agree) is gentler and more common than a flat "不 同意".

topics.title: Telling a story
topics.description: Sequencing past events with 着 and directional verbs

guide.intro: When you narrate a story you need ways to set the scene ("she was sitting"), describe motion ("he walked in"), and string events together. 着 handles ongoing states; directional complements like 上来 and 下去 handle motion in space.

sections.text: 着 — ongoing state
着 (zhe) attached to a verb means "in the state of doing". It's NOT the same as English -ing — 着 emphasizes a held position or background condition, often setting the scene.

rows.translation: He is standing. (in a standing state)
The door is open. (held open)

rows.source: 她 笑 着 说。
rows.translation: She said with a smile. (smiling-while-speaking)

sections.text: 着 vs 在: 在 means "actively doing right now" ("我 在 吃饭" — I'm eating). 着 means "in this state" ("门 开 着" — the door's open). For narration, 着 sets the scene; 在 reports a live action.
Directional complements: 上 / 下 / 进 / 出 / 来 / 去
Six little words combine into rich verbs of motion. Pair a base direction (up/down/in/out) with 来 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker).

rows.source: 他 走 进来 了。
rows.translation: He walked in.

rows.source: 她 跑 出去 了。
rows.translation: She ran out.
Please come up.

sections.text: Figurative directionals — 起来 / 下去 / 出来
Directional complements stretch beyond physical motion. Attached to non-motion verbs, they signal phase or aspect: starting, continuing, or coming-to-clarity.

rows: 看 起来 很 累 — looks tired

rows.source: 我 终于 想 出来 了。
rows.translation: I finally figured it out.

rows.source: 请 你 说 下 去。
rows.translation: Please keep talking.

rows.source: 他 突然 笑 起来 了。
rows.translation: He suddenly started to laugh.

sections.text: Sequencing words
A2's 然后 still works, but B1 stories add 先...再... (first...then...), 最后 (finally), 突然 (suddenly), and 后来 (afterward — for events further apart).

rows.source: 我 先 吃饭，再 看 电影。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiān chīfàn, zài kàn diànyǐng.
rows.translation: First I'll eat, then watch a movie.
It suddenly started to rain.

rows.source: 后来 他 搬 走 了。
rows.translation: Afterward, he moved away.

levels.name: B2 — Upper Intermediate
levels.description: Discuss abstract topics, defend opinions, and handle the news, the workplace, and contemporary Chinese culture.

topics.title: Expressing opinions
topics.description: Hedge, agree, push back, and stack reasons

guide.intro: At B2 you stop just stating opinions and start structuring them — adding nuance, layering reasons, and naming the side you fall on. Three patterns will carry most of your opinion-talk for the rest of your Chinese life: 不仅…而且 (not only…but also), 我觉得…比较 (I think…relatively), and 一方面…另一方面 (on one hand…on the other).

sections.text: 不仅…而且 — not only…but also

不仅 (bù jǐn) sets up the first half of a two-part claim, and 而且 (ér qiě) adds the second, usually stronger, point. The two halves can share a subject (which sits in front) or have different subjects (which sit after each particle).

rows.source: 他不仅会说中文，而且会说日语。
rows.pinyin: Tā bù jǐn huì shuō Zhōngwén, ér qiě huì shuō Rìyǔ.
rows.translation: He not only speaks Chinese, but also Japanese.

rows.source: 这家餐厅不仅便宜，而且很好吃。
rows.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng bù jǐn piányi, ér qiě hěn hǎo chī.
rows.translation: This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious.

rows.source: 不仅我喜欢他，而且我妹妹也喜欢他。
rows.pinyin: Bù jǐn wǒ xǐhuan tā, ér qiě wǒ mèimei yě xǐhuan tā.
rows.translation: Not only do I like him, but my sister does too.

sections.text: Common mistake: dropping 而且 and joining with a comma. In Mandarin, 不仅 always pairs with 而且 (or 也 / 还). "他不仅高，帅" sounds incomplete.
Softening: 我觉得 + 比较

比较 (bǐ jiào) means "relatively" or "fairly" — it takes the edge off an opinion the way "kind of" does in English. Pair it with 我觉得 (wǒ jué de, "I feel") for a polite, hedged tone that won't sound confrontational.

rows.source: 我觉得这个想法比较有意思。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ jué de zhè ge xiǎngfǎ bǐ jiào yǒu yì si.
rows.translation: I think this idea is fairly interesting.

rows.source: 我觉得他说的比较有道理。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ jué de tā shuō de bǐ jiào yǒu dào lǐ.
rows.translation: I think what he said makes a fair amount of sense.

sections.text: Two sides: 一方面…另一方面
Use 一方面 (yī fāng miàn)…另一方面 (lìng yī fāng miàn) to lay out two sides of the same issue — the closest Mandarin gets to "on one hand…on the other hand".

rows.source: 一方面工作很累，另一方面工资也不高。
rows.pinyin: Yī fāng miàn gōng zuò hěn lèi, lìng yī fāng miàn gōng zī yě bù gāo.
rows.translation: On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't great either.

lessons.title: I think, I feel

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between 觉得 and 认为?
options: 觉得 is more casual/feeling-based; 认为 is more considered/formal
觉得 means "think"; 认为 means "feel"

exercises.prompt: Build "I think this movie is really worth watching"

exercises.answer: I think what he said makes sense
acceptableAnswers: I believe what he said makes sense

exercises.prompt: Which is the most natural way to soften "I think it's expensive"?
exercises.explanation: 有点儿 (yǒu diǎnr) before an adjective is what does the softening — without it, 我觉得贵 is grammatical but blunt.

exercises.prompt: Build a more formal opinion: "I personally believe this idea is worth considering"
exercises.answer: 我 个人 认为 这个 想法 值得 考虑
exercises.explanation: 我个人认为 (wǒ gè rén rèn wéi) lifts the register — 个人 ("personally") plus 认为 sounds essay-like; 我觉得 would be the casual swap.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks 你觉得这家餐厅怎么样? Which reply HEDGES the most?
exercises.explanation: 还行吧 ("it's okay, I guess") plus 比较一般 ("relatively average") is the classic Chinese hedge — neither praising nor trashing.

exercises.prompt: "在我看来，这件事没那么简单" means ___
exercises.answer: In my view, this matter isn't that simple
acceptableAnswers: From my perspective, it's not that simple
The way I see it, this isn't so simple
In my opinion, this isn't that simple
exercises.explanation: 在我看来 (zài wǒ kàn lái) — "in my view". A common B2 opener for stating an opinion with a touch more weight than 我觉得.

exercises.prompt: the opinion-opener to its register

pairs.right: Stating a view: in my view
Older / literary: as I see it

exercises.prompt: Build "I think this question deserves more thought"
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 这个 问题 值得 多 想 一下

exercises.prompt: Pick the BLUNT version (avoid in polite settings):
options: 我觉得他说得有点儿不对
exercises.explanation: Bare 不对 with no hedge is direct to the point of rude. The other three all soften with 觉得, 不太, or 可能.

exercises.prompt: Convert casual "我觉得对" into a more formal/considered opinion. The blank should fill in: "我 ___ 这个观点是正确的"
exercises.explanation: Swap 觉得 → 认为 to lift register. 我认为这个观点是正确的 — "I believe this view is correct".

exercises.prompt: Tap the opener you hear
exercises.spokenText: 在 我 看 来
options: 在 我 看 来
在 我 来 看
看 来 我 在
我 看 在 来
exercises.answer: 在 我 看 来
exercises.explanation: 在我看来 (zài wǒ kàn lái) is a fixed four-syllable opener — the order is locked.

lessons.title: Not only, but also
lessons.description: Stack reasons with 不仅…而且

exercises.prompt: Build "This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious"
exercises.answer: 这家 餐厅 不仅 便宜 而且 很 好吃

exercises.prompt: Pick the best translation for "Not only do I like him, my sister also likes him":
options: 不仅我喜欢他，而且我妹妹也喜欢他
exercises.answer: 不仅我喜欢他，而且我妹妹也喜欢他

exercises.prompt: "他不仅聪明，而且很努力" means ___
exercises.answer: He is not only smart but also hardworking
acceptableAnswers: Not only is he smart, he is also hardworking
He's not only clever but also diligent

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 不仅 must pair with 而且 / 还 / 也. A bare comma is not enough — the second clause needs a connector.

exercises.prompt: 不仅 cannot pair with which of these?
exercises.explanation: 但是 introduces contrast ("but"). 不仅 needs an additive partner: 而且, 还, or 也.

exercises.prompt: Convert single-clause to compound: "He's hardworking and talented" → use 不仅...而且
exercises.answer: 他 不仅 努力 而且 有 才华

exercises.prompt: "这部电影不仅好看，___ 很有意义"
exercises.explanation: Any of 而且 / 还 / 也 completes the 不仅 pattern. The most common written choice is 而且.

exercises.prompt: Build "This phone is not only expensive but also doesn't have a good battery"
exercises.answer: 这 部 手机 不仅 贵 而且 电池 也 不 好

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "Not only does she sing, she also dances":
options: 她不仅会唱歌，还会跳舞
exercises.answer: 她不仅会唱歌，还会跳舞

exercises.prompt: "内卷不仅影响年轻人，还影响整个社会" means ___
exercises.answer: Involution doesn't only affect young people, it also affects the whole society
acceptableAnswers: Involution affects not only young people but the whole society
Not only does involution affect young people, it affects all of society
exercises.explanation: 内卷 — the cutthroat competition meme. The 不仅...还 frame stacks two scopes of impact.

exercises.prompt: Tap the connector you hear
exercises.explanation: 不仅 (bù jǐn) and 不但 (bù dàn) are near-synonyms — 不但 is slightly more spoken. 不过 means "however" and 不然 means "otherwise". Listen for the second syllable.

lessons.title: Agree & disagree
lessons.description: 同意, 反对, and the polite middle

exercises.prompt: the phrase to its meaning
Which is the most polite way to disagree?
exercises.explanation: Literally "I have a different view" — softer than a direct "you're wrong".

exercises.prompt: Build "I basically agree with your point of view"
exercises.answer: 我 基本 同意 你 的 看法

exercises.prompt: the agreement to its strength

pairs.right: Soft: I feel that way too

exercises.prompt: the disagreement to its tone

pairs.right: Pushback: I wouldn't put it that way

exercises.prompt: Build a hedged disagreement: "I'm not entirely sure I agree with this view"
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 确定 我 同意 这 个 看法

exercises.prompt: Your boss states a view in a meeting. Which response is appropriate?
options: 您的看法很有道理，不过我有一点不同意见
exercises.answer: 您的看法很有道理，不过我有一点不同意见
exercises.explanation: Concede first (有道理), then introduce disagreement with 不过 ("however") and a softener like 一点 — the standard formula for pushback in formal settings.

exercises.prompt: "话是这么说，可是…" means ___
exercises.explanation: 话是这么说，可是… is the most common spoken way to concede a point and pivot to your real objection.

exercises.prompt: Pick the strongest agreement:
Build a hedge: "To some extent, I agree with you"
exercises.answer: 在 某 种 程度 上 我 同意 你
exercises.explanation: 在某种程度上 — "to a certain degree" — the classic essay hedge before partial agreement.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 不 太 同意
options: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.explanation: 不太 + verb is the soft-disagreement frame. Hear it as a polite "not quite" rather than "not at all".

lessons.title: Two sides of an issue
lessons.description: 一方面…另一方面 and 既…又

exercises.prompt: What does "一方面…另一方面" mean?
options: On one hand… on the other hand
exercises.answer: On one hand… on the other hand

exercises.prompt: Build "On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't high"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工作 很 累 另一方面 工资 也 不 高

exercises.prompt: "她既聪明又漂亮" means ___
exercises.answer: She is both smart and beautiful
acceptableAnswers: She is smart as well as beautiful
exercises.explanation: 既…又 (jì…yòu) stacks two qualities of the same subject — "both…and".

exercises.prompt: Which best translates "It's expensive but worth it"?
Build "On one hand the salary is high, on the other hand the pressure is also great"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工资 很 高 另一方面 压力 也 很 大

exercises.prompt: "这个工作既稳定又有意思" means ___
exercises.answer: This job is both stable and interesting
acceptableAnswers: This job is stable and also interesting
It's a job that is both steady and interesting
exercises.explanation: 既...又 — stacks two qualities of one subject. 既 X 又 Y means "both X and Y".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 既 pairs with 又 (not 也). 既 X 又 Y is the locked frame.

exercises.prompt: Build "Studying abroad has both advantages and disadvantages"
exercises.answer: 出国 留学 既 有 好处 又 有 坏处

exercises.prompt: the two-sided pattern

pairs.right: On one hand…on the other (separate clauses)

exercises.prompt: "凡事都有两面" (fán shì dōu yǒu liǎng miàn) means ___
acceptableAnswers: There are two sides to everything
exercises.explanation: A common B2 set phrase to open a balanced opinion. 凡事 = every matter.

exercises.prompt: Build "Although AI is convenient, it also brings problems"
exercises.answer: 虽然 人工智能 很 方便 但是 也 带 来 一些 问题

exercises.prompt: Pick the most balanced essay-style opening:
options: 凡事都有两面：一方面…另一方面…
exercises.answer: 凡事都有两面：一方面…另一方面…
exercises.explanation: Balanced essays in Chinese almost always open with 凡事都有两面 or a similar two-sides formula before laying out 一方面 / 另一方面.

lessons.title: Dialogue: Discussing a film at a coffee shop
lessons.description: Hedge your film opinions, half-agree, and recommend with a caveat

exercises.prompt: Coffee-shop chat about a film you saw last night

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 你昨天看的那部电影怎么样？(Nǐ zuótiān kàn de nà bù diànyǐng zěnmeyàng?)
turns.spokenText: 你昨天看的那部电影怎么样？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Soften your opinion (hedging).
options: 我觉得剧情比较拖沓，不过演技不错。(Wǒ juéde jùqíng bǐjiào tuōtà, búguò yǎnjì búcuò.)
剧情绝对烂透了，没什么好说的。(Jùqíng juéduì làn tòule, méi shénme hǎo shuō de.)
电影虽然好，因此结尾差。(Diànyǐng suīrán hǎo, yīncǐ jiéwěi chà.)
turns.answer: 我觉得剧情比较拖沓，不过演技不错。(Wǒ juéde jùqíng bǐjiào tuōtà, búguò yǎnjì búcuò.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 对，我也觉得节奏有点慢。(Duì, wǒ yě juéde jiézòu yǒudiǎn màn.)
turns.spokenText: 对，我也觉得节奏有点慢。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Half-agree, then add a nuance.
options: 我部分同意，不过那些慢镜头反而很有味道。(Wǒ bùfèn tóngyì, búguò nàxiē màn jìngtóu fǎn'ér hěn yǒu wèidào.)
完全同意而且非常好。(Wánquán tóngyì érqiě fēicháng hǎo.)
不知道我无所谓的吧。(Bù zhīdào wǒ wúsuǒwèi de ba.)
turns.answer: 我部分同意，不过那些慢镜头反而很有味道。(Wǒ bùfèn tóngyì, búguò nàxiē màn jìngtóu fǎn'ér hěn yǒu wèidào.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 说得也是。导演想表达的主题你看懂了吗？(Shuō de yěshì. Dǎoyǎn xiǎng biǎodá de zhǔtí nǐ kàndǒng le ma?)
turns.spokenText: 说得也是。导演想表达的主题你看懂了吗？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in the hedge — 'I feel maybe'.
turns.after: 是在讲家庭的疏离感。(Wǒ ___ shì zài jiǎng jiātíng de shūlí gǎn.)
turns.answer: 觉得大概

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 嗯，那种感觉确实贯穿全片。(Èn, nà zhǒng gǎnjué quèshí guànchuān quánpiàn.)
turns.spokenText: 嗯，那种感觉确实贯穿全片。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Recommend it — but with a caveat.
options: 推荐看，不过得有耐心，节奏比较慢。(Tuījiàn kàn, búguò děi yǒu nàixīn, jiézòu bǐjiào màn.)
强烈不推荐，肯定别看了。(Qiángliè bù tuījiàn, kěndìng bié kàn le.)
可以看也可以不看反正都行。(Kěyǐ kàn yě kěyǐ bù kàn fǎnzhèng dōu xíng.)
turns.answer: 推荐看，不过得有耐心，节奏比较慢。(Tuījiàn kàn, búguò děi yǒu nàixīn, jiézòu bǐjiào màn.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 好，我下周找时间去看。(Hǎo, wǒ xià zhōu zhǎo shíjiān qù kàn.)
turns.spokenText: 好，我下周找时间去看。

topics.title: News & current events
topics.description: Read a headline, summarize what happened, give your take

lessons.title: News vocabulary
lessons.description: 新闻, 报道, 媒体 — the building blocks

exercises.prompt: the term to its meaning
What does "头条新闻" (tóu tiáo xīn wén) mean?
exercises.explanation: 头条 literally means "top entry" — but it's also the name of a hugely popular news app, 今日头条.

exercises.prompt: "据报道" (jù bào dào) means ___
the news-vocabulary term
What does "自媒体" (zì méi tǐ) mean?
exercises.explanation: 自媒体 — literally "self-media". The Weibo / WeChat public accounts ecosystem; contrasted with 传统媒体 (traditional media).

exercises.prompt: online vs traditional media term
Build "This piece of news got onto the trending list (热搜)"
exercises.answer: 这 条 新闻 上 了 热搜

exercises.prompt: "独家报道" (dú jiā bào dào) means ___
What does "假新闻" (jiǎ xīn wén) mean?
Build "Today's headline news is about education reform"
exercises.answer: 今天 的 头条 新闻 是 关于 教育 改革

exercises.prompt: Tap the news vocab you hear
exercises.spokenText: 突 发 新 闻
options: 突 发 新 闻
头 条 新 闻
突 然 新 闻
热 门 新 闻
exercises.answer: 突 发 新 闻
exercises.explanation: 突发 (tū fā) — "suddenly occurring" — pairs with 新闻 to form the breaking-news idiom. Don't confuse with 头条 (headline) or 突然 (suddenly).

exercises.prompt: Which is the most NEWS-REGISTER way to start a sentence?
options: 我朋友说今天那个事儿…
exercises.explanation: 据相关媒体报道 — "according to relevant media reports" — the standard news opener. The casual options would never appear in a print or anchor segment.

lessons.title: What happened?
lessons.description: 发生, 引起, 影响 — narrating events

exercises.prompt: What does "发生" (fā shēng) mean?
Build "This event has had a big impact on society"
exercises.answer: 这件 事 对 社会 有 很大 的 影响

exercises.prompt: "引起广泛关注" (yǐn qǐ guǎng fàn guān zhù) means ___
What does "事故" (shì gù) mean?
the verb to its meaning
Convert active to passive: "The accident was caused by drunk driving" using 被
exercises.answer: 这 起 事故 是 由 酒驾 造成 的
exercises.explanation: News register prefers 是…由…造成的 over plain 被. 由 marks the agent. 起 is the measure word for incidents.

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "This decision will have far-reaching effects":
options: 这个决定会产生深远的影响
exercises.answer: 这个决定会产生深远的影响
exercises.explanation: 产生影响 — "produce an impact" — is the standard collocation. 深远 ("far-reaching") is essay-register.

exercises.prompt: "事件 (shì jiàn) 引发了 公众 的 关注" means ___
acceptableAnswers: The incident set off public attention
exercises.explanation: 引发 = trigger / set off — slightly stronger and more news-y than 引起.

exercises.prompt: Build "The incident drew widespread attention from society"
exercises.answer: 这 件 事 引起 了 社会 的 广泛 关注

exercises.prompt: Pick the news-headline-style passive: "The suspect was arrested":
exercises.explanation: Headlines use formal verbs: 逮捕 (arrest) over casual 抓. 警方 over casual 警察.

exercises.prompt: "目前已造成多人受伤" (mù qián yǐ zào chéng duō rén shòu shāng) means ___
exercises.answer: So far it has caused multiple injuries
acceptableAnswers: As of now, multiple people have been injured
Currently it has caused several people to be injured
exercises.explanation: 目前 (currently) is the news-register version of 现在. 已 (already) is its 已经 equivalent. Strip the casualness for an anchor's voice.

exercises.prompt: Tap the verb you hear
exercises.explanation: 导致 (dǎo zhì) is more clinical and explanatory; 引起 (yǐn qǐ) is more general; 造成 (zào chéng) emphasizes negative outcomes. All three appear in news but the verb you hear here is 导致.

lessons.title: Politics & society
lessons.description: 政府, 政策, 社会 — the public sphere

exercises.prompt: the term to its meaning
Build "The government has launched a new policy"
exercises.answer: 政府 出 台 了 一 项 新 政策

exercises.prompt: "经济发展" (jīng jì fā zhǎn) means ___
the public-sphere term
What does "出台" (chū tái) mean in the context of policy?
exercises.explanation: 出台 here is news-register for "launch". 政府出台新政策 = the government rolls out a new policy.

exercises.prompt: Build "This policy aims to support young people in starting businesses"
exercises.answer: 这 项 政策 旨在 支持 年轻 人 创业
exercises.explanation: 旨在 (zhǐ zài) — "aims to / is intended to" — formal news collocation. 项 is the measure word for policies.

exercises.prompt: "贫富差距" (pín fù chā jù) means ___
exercises.answer: The wealth gap / gap between rich and poor

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "The new policy will affect millions of people":
options: 新政策将影响数百万人
exercises.answer: 新政策将影响数百万人
exercises.explanation: 将 is the news-register "will". 数百万 = several million.

exercises.prompt: Build "The government has paid great attention to this issue"
exercises.answer: 政府 对 这 个 问题 非常 重视
exercises.explanation: 重视 — "attach importance to / take seriously". 对...重视 is the standard frame.

exercises.prompt: casual to news-register equivalent
"这是一个值得深思的问题" means ___
exercises.answer: This is a question worth deep reflection
acceptableAnswers: This is a topic worth pondering
This is an issue worth thinking about deeply
exercises.explanation: 深思 — "deep reflection" — common in editorials and opinion pieces.

exercises.prompt: Tap the formal connector you hear (anchor delivery)
exercises.explanation: 由于 is the news/written equivalent of 因为. 由此 ("from this") is a follow-on connector. Listen for the second syllable.

lessons.title: Reading a headline
lessons.description: Compress meaning the way headlines do

exercises.prompt: Headlines often drop particles. "北京 今日 大雪" means:
exercises.explanation: Headlines compress: no 有, no 了 — the reader fills in the verb.

exercises.prompt: Build "According to reports, the issue has been resolved"
exercises.answer: 据 报道 问题 已经 解决 了

exercises.prompt: "最新消息" (zuì xīn xiāo xi) means ___
"专家表示" (zhuān jiā biǎo shì) means:
Tap the headline you hear (read aloud, news-style)
exercises.spokenText: 据 报道 问题 已经 解决 了
options: 据 报道 问题 已经 解决 了
据 报道 政府 已经 决定 了
据 调查 问题 还 没 解决
据 媒体 报道 经济 增长 了
exercises.answer: 据 报道 问题 已经 解决 了
exercises.explanation: Headlines are spoken in clipped, declarative cadence. Tune your ear to the opening 据报道 ("according to reports") and the verb-final 解决了 ("resolved").

exercises.prompt: Compress to a headline: "The economy is growing this year" → headline style (drop 在/了)
exercises.answer: 今年 经济 持续 增长
exercises.explanation: Headlines drop aspect particles and choose a punchier verb (持续 = continuously). Casual full-form would be: 今年经济在持续增长.

exercises.prompt: "暴雨袭击北京" — pick the best translation:
exercises.explanation: 袭击 (xí jī, "strike / attack") is favored in headline metaphors for storms, fires, and disasters.

exercises.prompt: "再创新高" (zài chuàng xīn gāo) means ___
exercises.explanation: A stock collocation in finance and economics headlines: 再创新高 = the indicator/price hits another record.

exercises.prompt: the headline verb
Which is HEADLINE register, not casual?
options: 刚刚听说啊，那个公司倒了
你听说了吗，那个公司不行了
exercises.explanation: 宣告 (declare) and 破产 (bankruptcy) are formal verbs. Headlines compress and dignify what casual speech would render with 不行了 / 倒了.

exercises.prompt: Build a headline: "Two countries sign trade agreement" (drop particles)
exercises.answer: 两 国 签署 贸易 协议

exercises.prompt: Tap the headline cadence you hear (anchor delivery)
exercises.spokenText: 专 家 表 示 此 事 影 响 深 远
options: 专 家 表 示 此 事 影 响 深 远
专 家 表 示 这 件 事 影 响 很 大
专 家 说 这 件 事 没 什 么 影 响
新 闻 报 道 这 件 事 的 影 响
exercises.answer: 专 家 表 示 此 事 影 响 深 远
exercises.explanation: Listen for 此事 (this matter) instead of 这件事 — both mean the same but 此 is news/written register only. Anchors deliver these compressed forms.

lessons.title: Generations & society in the news
lessons.description: 80后, 北漂, 趋势 — vocabulary for stories about people

exercises.prompt: the term

pairs.right: Young migrant chasing work in Beijing

exercises.prompt: What does "趋势" (qū shì) mean?
Build "More and more young people choose not to get married"
exercises.answer: 越 来 越 多 的 年轻 人 选择 不 结婚

exercises.prompt: "我们这一代" (wǒ men zhè yī dài) means ___
Best translation for "This is a very common phenomenon today":
options: 这是现在很普遍的现象
exercises.answer: 这是现在很普遍的现象

exercises.prompt: the social-trend term
Build "China is becoming an aging society"
exercises.answer: 中国 正在 成为 一 个 老龄化 社会

exercises.prompt: "内卷已经成为这一代人的关键词" means ___
exercises.answer: Involution has become the keyword of this generation
acceptableAnswers: Involution has become a keyword for this generation
Involution is now the watchword of this generation
exercises.explanation: 内卷 — buzzword for cutthroat competition. 关键词 = keyword. Common phrasing in op-eds about young Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Pick the news-style writing — "More and more young people are choosing to lie flat":
options: 越来越多的年轻人选择躺平
现在年轻人都不干活儿
exercises.answer: 越来越多的年轻人选择躺平
exercises.explanation: 越来越多的 + N + 选择 + V is the news-essay frame for trend reporting. The other options drift into casual register.

exercises.prompt: Build "Behind this trend lie complex social factors"
exercises.answer: 这 种 趋势 背后 有 复杂 的 社会 因素
exercises.explanation: Standard editorial frame: 这种趋势背后 + 有 + adj + 因素. 因素 (factor) over 原因 (reason) signals analytic register.

exercises.prompt: "我们这一代面临着前所未有的压力" means ___
acceptableAnswers: Our generation is facing pressure like never before
This generation of ours faces pressure that's never been seen before
exercises.explanation: 前所未有 (qián suǒ wèi yǒu) — "unprecedented". Stock B2 essay phrase.

exercises.prompt: Tap the slang term you hear
exercises.explanation: 躺平 (tǎng píng, lying flat) — the opt-out meme. Listen for the falling tone on 躺 followed by rising 平.

topics.title: Environment & climate
topics.description: Pollution, recycling, climate change — and the more you do, the more it helps

guide.intro: 越…越 (yuè…yuè) is one of the most useful patterns at B2 — and one of the prettiest. It means "the more X, the more Y". You'll hear it everywhere from weather reports to op-eds. This topic uses environmental issues as the playground for it.

sections.text: 越…越 — the more…the more
The pattern is fixed: 越 + verb/adjective, 越 + verb/adjective. The two halves can share a subject (which sits at the front) or have different subjects.

rows.pinyin: Tiān qì yuè lái yuè rè.
rows.translation: The weather is getting hotter and hotter.

rows.pinyin: Tā yuè shuō yuè shēng qì.
rows.translation: The more he talked, the angrier he got.
The rain came down heavier and heavier.

sections.text: 越来越 — getting X-er
越来越 (yuè lái yuè) is the most common form: "more and more". It always sits in front of an adjective or stative verb, and signals a trend over time.

rows.pinyin: Kōng qì yuè lái yuè chà.
rows.translation: The air is getting worse and worse.

rows.pinyin: Huán bǎo yuè lái yuè zhòng yào.
rows.translation: Environmental protection is getting more and more important.

sections.text: Don't add 很 between 越来越 and the adjective. "越来越很热" is wrong — 越来越 already does the intensifying.
Two-subject form
When the two halves have different subjects, both subjects appear inside the pattern, after each 越:

rows.source: 天气越冷，我越想吃火锅。
rows.pinyin: Tiān qì yuè lěng, wǒ yuè xiǎng chī huǒ guō.
rows.translation: The colder the weather, the more I want hotpot.

lessons.title: The more, the more

exercises.prompt: What does "天气越来越热" mean?
options: The weather is getting hotter and hotter

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 越来越 already intensifies — adding 很 is double-marking.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: Same rule: 越来越 cannot be paired with another intensifier like 非常 or 很. Drop the 非常 — 他越来越努力 is correct.

exercises.prompt: Build "The colder the weather, the more I want to drink hot tea" (two-subject 越...越)
exercises.answer: 天气 越 冷 我 越 想 喝 热 茶

exercises.prompt: "环保意识越来越强" means ___
exercises.answer: Environmental awareness is getting stronger and stronger

exercises.prompt: the 越 frame to its meaning

pairs.right: The more X, the more Y

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "The earlier we act, the better":
exercises.explanation: 越 X 越 Y is the locked frame. 越早 (the earlier) + 越好 (the better) — a stock recommendation phrase.

天 气 比 较 热
exercises.answer: 天 气 越 来 越 热
exercises.explanation: 越来越 + adj is one of the most common B2 patterns spoken at conversational speed. Listen for the rising-falling cadence on 越来越.

exercises.prompt: What does "垃圾分类" (lā jī fēn lèi) mean?

exercises.prompt: the trash category
"我们应该保护环境" means ___

Best translation for "More and more people are using reusable cups":

exercises.answer: 越来越多的人开始用环保杯

有 害 垃 圾

lessons.title: Climate change in conversation
lessons.description: Stitch the vocabulary into real sentences

exercises.prompt: Build "Climate change is one of the most serious problems today"
exercises.answer: 气候 变化 是 今天 最 严重 的 问题 之一

exercises.prompt: Which best translates "We should ride bikes more and drive cars less"?
options: 我们应该多骑自行车，少开车
exercises.answer: 我们应该多骑自行车，少开车
exercises.explanation: 多 + verb / 少 + verb is a clean way to recommend more/less of an action.

exercises.prompt: "节约用水" (jié yuē yòng shuǐ) means ___
Tap the sentence you hear
options: 今天 比 昨天 冷
今天 不 太 冷
exercises.explanation: 比较 (bǐ jiào, "relatively") and 比 (bǐ, "compared to") sound nearly identical — but 比 always needs a comparison object after it (比 X), while 比较 just modifies an adjective.

exercises.prompt: Build "Today is five degrees hotter than yesterday" (比 + numerical comparison)
exercises.answer: 今天 比 昨天 热 五 度
exercises.explanation: 比 + numerical comparison: A 比 B + adj + amount. The amount goes AFTER the adjective: 高 五 厘米 (5 cm taller), 热 五 度 (5 degrees hotter), 大 三 岁 (3 years older).

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "He is five centimeters taller than me":
exercises.explanation: Pattern: A 比 B + adjective + number/amount. The amount of difference always comes after the adjective.

exercises.prompt: Build "To protect the planet, we should start with small things"
exercises.answer: 为 了 保护 地球 我们 应该 从 小事 做 起

exercises.prompt: "低碳生活" (dī tàn shēng huó) means ___
Best translation for "If we don't act, the consequences will be severe":
options: 如果我们不行动，后果将会很严重
exercises.answer: 如果我们不行动，后果将会很严重
exercises.explanation: 如果...将会 — "if...will". 将 (formal future) plus 会 doubles up the future-modal in essay style.

exercises.prompt: Build "Even if one person's effort is small, it can still change the world" (即使...也)
exercises.answer: 即使 一 个 人 的 力量 很 小 也 能 改变 世界
